chunks: Lie down between the two rak'ahs of Fajr and the two rak'ahs of the morning prayer on your right side facing the qiblah, and say in your reclining: “I have held fast to the firm handhold of Allah, which has no breaking apart, and I have sought protection in the strong rope of Allah. I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the wicked of the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the wicked of the jinn and humankind. Glory be to the Lord of the morning, the splitter of the dawn. Glory be to the Lord of the morning, the splitter of the dawn. Glory be to the Lord of the morning, the splitter of the dawn.”

Then say: “In the Name of Allah, I have placed my side down for Allah. I have consigned my affair to Allah. I seek my need from Allah. I have relied upon Allah. Allah is sufficient for me, and excellent is the Trustee. And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Indeed Allah accomplishes His command. Allah has appointed a measure for everything. O Allah, whoever begins the morning with his need directed to a created being, then indeed my need and my desire are toward You.”
And recite five verses from the end of Surat Al 'Imran: “Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...” up to His saying: “Indeed, You do not fail in the promise.”
And send blessings upon Muhammad and his family one hundred times, for indeed it...

key_terms.آلِ عِمْرَانَ: Surat Al 'Imran, from whose final verses recitation is instructed
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The direction of prayer toward which one faces
key_terms.اِضْطَجِعْ: Lie down or recline in the prescribed devotional manner
key_terms.بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ الْمَتِينِ: The strong rope of Allah, signifying divine protection and steadfast adherence
key_terms.بِعُرْوَةِ اللَّهِ الْوُثْقَى: The firm handhold of Allah, meaning secure attachment and reliance upon Him
key_terms.تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ: I have placed my trust and reliance upon Allah
key_terms.قَدْرًا: A fixed measure or decree appointed by Allah for all things

ai.seo_question: What should be recited when reclining between the two rak'ahs of Fajr and the morning prayer?
ai.summary: This text teaches a recommended devotional practice between the two rak'ahs of Fajr and the morning prayer: reclining toward the qiblah, reciting words of reliance upon Allah, seeking refuge from evil, and remembering His power over all affairs. It also connects this act of worship with Qur'anic recitation from the end of Surat Al 'Imran and repeated salawat upon Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his family, emphasizing tawakkul, protection, and morning devotion.
